items.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We stopped in Chicago, where I met Muggsy Spanier and so many musicians for the first time and set up what ended up being the first jazz album that anyone had ever recorded as an album.

ctx.x: Which has now bed and breakfast.

That’s right, bed and breakfast, except they didn’t give you breakfast. So that was nice, because we got to meet people in every state. The interesting thing about the trip also was that Marshall, who knew America very well of course, knew where to make little side trips and find Mark Twain’s home and things like that. He routed us so that we went through Emporia, Kansas, and dropped in on Mr. White, the editor of the Emporia Gazette. He was a very influential editor at that time, and a liberal, which I guess is…
